papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proves an NLTS-type lower bound for Z2-symmetric circuits, derives limits on constant-level QAOA for MaxCut, and proposes the recursive QAOA (RQAOA).

assertions.value: The authors define a local Hamiltonian as a sum of interaction terms that each act non-trivially on O(1) qubits, and require each term to have operator norm O(1) and each qubit to be involved in O(1) terms.
quotes: A local Hamiltonian is a sum of interaction terms acting non-trivially on O(1) qubits each.
We require that each term has operator norm O(1) and each qubit is involved in O(1) terms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own definition of a local Hamiltonian on page 1.

assertions.value: The authors call a local Hamiltonian Z2-symmetric if all interaction terms commute with the tensor product of Pauli-X on all n qubits, and a circuit U Z2-symmetric if it obeys U X^n = X^n U. They do not impose the symmetry on the individual gates of U.
quotes: A local Hamiltonian is said to be Z2symmetric if all interaction terms commute with X⊗n, where X is the single-qubit Pauli-X operator.
U X⊗n = X⊗nU .
We do not impose the symmetry on the individual gates of U , though this will naturally be the case in many interesting examples

assertions.value: The authors call a state of n qubits Z2-symmetric if applying X on all n qubits returns the state or its negative.
quotes: Finally, let us say that a state Ψ of n qubits is Z2-symmetric if X⊗nΨ = ±Ψ.

assertions.value: The authors state that the question whether there are local Hamiltonians for which any low-energy state is non-trivial was formalized by Freedman and Hastings as the No Low-energy Trivial States (NLTS) conjecture.

Formalized by Freedman and Hastings [6], this is known as the No Lowenergy Trivial States (NLTS) conjecture.

assertions.value: The authors state that for cost functions with interactions among three or more variables, mean values of Pauli operators on the QAOA state can be approximately computed with a Monte Carlo method due to Van den Nest.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Monte Carlo simulator has runtime scaling polynomially with the number of qubits, the number of terms in the cost function, and the inverse error tolerance, and requires no restrictions on the depth of the variational circuit.

assertions.value: The authors state that QAOA requires few-qubit measurements to estimate the variational energy as well as a final n-qubit measurement, whereas RQAOA only needs few-qubit measurements to estimate mean values of individual terms in the cost function.

In contrast, RQAOA only needs few-qubit measurements to estimate mean values of individual terms in the cost function.
